title: Eighth Word Applying The Symbols In The Comparison General Principle

questions.question: If a person wants to be like the happy brother, what should he listen to and follow?
questions.answer: He should listen to the Qur’an and obey it.

questions.question: What does the passage say a person can understand after learning from this comparison?
questions.answer: He can match it to religion, the world, people, and belief in Allah.

questions.question: In the comparison, what does the good brother stand for?
questions.answer: A believing soul and a good heart.

questions.question: In the comparison, what does the other brother stand for?
questions.answer: An unbelieving soul and a bad heart.

questions.question: What does the right-hand road mean?
questions.answer: The way of the Qur’an and belief in Allah.

questions.question: What does the left-hand road mean?
questions.answer: The way of rebellion and denial.

questions.question: What does the garden on the road stand for?
questions.answer: A person’s short life in the world with people, where good and bad are mixed together.

questions.question: What kind of person is called sensible in the passage?
questions.answer: A person who takes the good and leaves the bad.

questions.question: What happens to the sensible person when he chooses the good?
questions.answer: He goes on with a peaceful heart.

questions.question: What does the desert represent?
questions.answer: The earth and this world.

questions.question: What does the lion represent?
questions.answer: Death and the set time to die.

questions.question: What does the well represent?
questions.answer: A person’s body and the time of his life.

questions.question: What does the well’s depth point to?
questions.answer: A usual life span of sixty years.

questions.question: What does the tree represent?
questions.answer: The time of life and the living part of life.

questions.question: What do the white and black animals represent?
questions.answer: Night and day.

questions.question: What does the dragon represent?
questions.answer: The way to the next world and the hereafter place, with its mouth meaning the grave.

questions.question: For a believer, what is the grave like?
questions.answer: It is like a door from a prison to a garden.

questions.question: What do the poisonous little creatures represent?
questions.answer: The troubles and hardships of this world.

questions.question: For a believer, what can those hardships be like?
questions.answer: Gentle warnings and mercies from Allah to keep him awake and careful.

questions.question: What do the fruits on the tree represent?
questions.answer: The blessings of this world that point to the blessings of the hereafter.

questions.question: Why are those fruits also called samples and invitations?
questions.answer: Because they give a small taste and call people toward the fruits of Paradise.

questions.question: What does one tree giving many kinds of fruit show?
questions.answer: Allah’s power and rule.

questions.question: What is the talisman in the story compared to?
questions.answer: The secret of why creation was made.

questions.question: Through what is that secret understood?
questions.answer: Through belief.

questions.question: What is the key named in the passage?
questions.answer: Saying that there is no god but Allah, and that Allah alone is the Ever-Living and Self-Subsisting.

questions.question: What does the dragon’s mouth turning into a garden door show for believers?
questions.answer: It shows that the grave opens to everlasting life and Paradise for them.

questions.question: What does death become for people of guidance and the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It becomes a way to meet loved ones, go to their true home, and receive rest and reward.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is one more meaning of death for believers?
questions.answer: It is relief from the hard duties and tests of life.

questions.question: At the start of the passage, what choice is the listener asked to make?
questions.answer: To be like the fortunate brother, not the unfortunate one.

questions.question: What must a person do with the Qur’an besides listening to it?
questions.answer: He must obey it, hold to it, and live by it.

questions.question: After understanding the story, what four big things can a person connect it to?
questions.answer: Religion, the world, man, and belief in Allah.

questions.question: What does the first brother stand for inside a person?
questions.answer: A believing spirit and a righteous heart.

questions.question: Which road is the road of faith?
questions.answer: The right road.

questions.question: Which road is the road of turning away from truth?
questions.answer: The left road.

questions.question: What does the roadside garden teach about life with other people?
questions.answer: That life has both clean and unclean things, and both good and bad.

questions.question: What wise rule should a person follow in that mixed life?
questions.answer: Take the clean, pleasant part and leave the troubling part.

questions.question: What reward comes from following that rule?
questions.answer: Calmness in the heart.

questions.question: What place in the story means the world we live in?
questions.answer: The desert.

questions.question: In the explanation, what does the lion mean?
questions.answer: Death and the time fixed for it.

questions.question: What two things does the well point to?
questions.answer: The human body and the length of life.

questions.question: What does the number sixty in the well suggest?
questions.answer: A normal human life of sixty years.

questions.question: What does the tree in the well stand for?
questions.answer: Life’s period and its support.

questions.question: What do the two root-gnawing creatures stand for?
questions.answer: The passing of night and day.

questions.question: What does the dragon’s mouth stand for?
questions.answer: The grave and the road to the next life.

questions.question: How is the grave different for a believer?
questions.answer: It is like an opening to a garden, not a trap.

questions.question: What are the stinging harmful creatures compared to?
questions.answer: Worldly troubles and disasters.

questions.question: How can those troubles help a believer?
questions.answer: They can wake him up and stop him from becoming careless.

questions.question: What do the fruits of the tree teach about worldly blessings?
questions.answer: They are signs and small examples of the blessings of the next life.

questions.question: What does one tree carrying many kinds of fruit prove?
questions.answer: It points to Allah’s amazing power and ownership.

questions.question: What mystery does the talisman symbolize?
questions.answer: The reason and purpose behind creation.

questions.question: What opens that mystery?
questions.answer: Faith and the words of tawhid.

questions.question: What is one of the key phrases given in the passage?
questions.answer: There is no god but Allah.

questions.question: For people who reject guidance, what is the grave like?
questions.answer: It is like a narrow, scary prison.

questions.question: For people of the Qur’an and faith, what does the grave open to?
questions.answer: Everlasting life and the gardens of Paradise.

questions.question: How is death described for people of guidance?
questions.answer: It is a meeting with loved ones, a journey home, and a time of rest and reward.

questions.question: Who is being spoken to along with the nafs in the first lines?
questions.answer: The person listening to the story.

questions.question: What should someone do if he does not want the sad ending of the unhappy brother?
questions.answer: He should follow the Qur’an.

questions.question: What can a person work out for himself after the main meanings are shown?
questions.answer: The smaller details.

questions.question: In this explanation, what kind of inner life does the fortunate brother show?
questions.answer: A faithful soul and a good heart.

questions.question: What kind of inner life does the unfortunate brother show?
questions.answer: A soul without faith and a spoiled heart.

questions.question: What does the road on the right teach?
questions.answer: It teaches the path of the Qur’an and iman.

questions.question: What does the road on the left teach?
questions.answer: It teaches the path of disobedience and denying truth.

questions.question: Why is the garden a good picture for worldly life?
questions.answer: Because worldly life has nice things and bad things together.

questions.question: How does a wise person deal with that mixed garden of life?
questions.answer: He chooses the good part and leaves the harmful part.

questions.question: What feeling does that wise choice bring?
questions.answer: Peace in the heart.

questions.question: What does the desert stand for in the lesson?
questions.answer: The earth and this passing world.

questions.question: What does the lion remind people of?
questions.answer: Death and the time appointed by Allah.

questions.question: What does the well show about a human being?
questions.answer: It shows his body and the span of his life.

questions.question: Why is the depth of the well important in the meaning?
questions.answer: It points to an ordinary life span of sixty years.

questions.question: What does the tree stand for in a person’s life?
questions.answer: The lifetime and the base of living.

questions.question: What do the black and white animals teach us about time?
questions.answer: That night and day keep passing.

questions.question: What does the dragon teach about what comes after this world?
questions.answer: It teaches about the way to the hereafter and the grave.

questions.question: What change happens to the grave for a believer in this meaning?
questions.answer: It becomes like a doorway to a garden.

questions.question: What are the poisonous creatures around the person like in real life?
questions.answer: They are like troubles and painful events in this world.

questions.question: Why are those troubles called a mercy for believers?
questions.answer: Because they warn them and keep them from forgetting Allah.

questions.question: What are worldly blessings meant to point people toward?
questions.answer: The blessings of the hereafter and Paradise.

questions.question: What does the many-fruited tree say about Allah?
questions.answer: That His power can do what no one else can do.

questions.question: What does making many things from one thing show?
questions.answer: It shows Allah’s special power as Creator.

questions.question: What does making one thing from many things also show?
questions.answer: It also shows Allah’s unique power and wisdom.

questions.question: What is the talisman’s meaning in the lesson?
questions.answer: The hidden purpose of creation.

questions.question: What words are given as the key to that meaning?
questions.answer: The words of Allah’s oneness and His perfect life and self-subsistence.

questions.question: What does the lion becoming gentle show about death for believers?
questions.answer: That death becomes a helper, not an enemy.

questions.question: What good things does death bring to believers in the passage?
questions.answer: Meeting loved ones, reaching their real home, reward, and rest.

questions.question: What does the passage tell a person to do if he wants the good brother’s path?
questions.answer: He should listen to the Qur’an and live by it.

questions.question: After understanding the story, what can a person compare it with?
questions.answer: The truths about religion, the world, human life, and faith in Allah.

questions.question: Which brother stands for faith and a clean heart?
questions.answer: The fortunate brother.

questions.question: Which brother stands for lack of faith and a ruined heart?
questions.answer: The unfortunate brother.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the right road?
questions.answer: It is the path of the Qur’an and belief in Allah.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the left road?
questions.answer: It is the path of rebellion and denial.

questions.question: What does the garden show about life among people?
questions.answer: It shows that life contains both good and bad things together.

questions.question: What simple rule helps a person in that kind of life?
questions.answer: Choose the clear good and leave the dirty or upsetting part.

questions.question: What does the passage say this wise person gains?
questions.answer: A calm and settled heart.

questions.question: What larger place is shown by the desert?
questions.answer: This earth and worldly life.

questions.question: What event in every person’s life is shown by the lion?
questions.answer: Death.

questions.question: What does the set time with the lion mean too?
questions.answer: A person’s appointed end.

questions.question: What does the well symbolize about human life?
questions.answer: The body and the lifetime inside it.

questions.question: What does the measure of sixty yards symbolize?
questions.answer: A normal life of about sixty years.

questions.question: What part of life is shown by the tree?
questions.answer: The length of life and what life depends on.

questions.question: Why are there two animals at the roots in the meaning?
questions.answer: Because they stand for day and night.

questions.question: What is the dragon in the explanation?
questions.answer: The way to the Intermediate Realm and the hereafter, with the grave as its opening.

questions.question: How is that opening different for a believer?
questions.answer: It becomes a door into a garden.

questions.question: What real-life things are like the poisonous vermin?
questions.answer: Calamities and troubles in the world.

questions.question: What kind of gift can those troubles be for a believer?
questions.answer: Merciful reminders that keep him from heedlessness.

questions.question: What are the fruits on the tree really pointing to?
questions.answer: The blessings of the next life.

questions.question: Besides being signs, what else are those fruits called in the passage?
questions.answer: Samples and invitations.

questions.question: What does one tree having many fruits tell us about Allah’s rule?
questions.answer: It shows His lordship, power, and sovereignty.

questions.question: What special mystery is called the talisman?
questions.answer: The mystery of why creation was made.

questions.question: What solves that mystery?
questions.answer: The mystery of belief.

questions.question: What key statement comes first in the passage?
questions.answer: There is no god but Allah.

questions.question: For people who go against guidance, how is the grave described?
questions.answer: As a painful and narrow place like a dungeon.

questions.question: For believers, what is death at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: A way to go home, meet loved ones, gain reward, and rest from hardship.

questions.question: What warning and advice are given to the listener at the beginning?
questions.answer: Do not be like the unfortunate brother; follow the Qur’an.

questions.question: What should a person do with the Qur’an’s commands?
questions.answer: Obey them and hold tightly to them.

questions.question: If someone understands this comparison well, what can he begin to understand better?
questions.answer: Big truths about religion, the world, people, and faith in Allah.

questions.question: What does one brother represent in a good way?
questions.answer: Faith and a righteous heart.

questions.question: What does the other brother represent in a bad way?
questions.answer: Unbelief and a corrupted heart.

questions.question: Which road is the road of belief?
questions.answer: The road on the right.

questions.question: Which road is the road of refusing truth?
questions.answer: The road on the left.

questions.question: Why is the garden compared to human life in society?
questions.answer: Because both have good and bad things mixed together.

questions.question: What should a smart person do when good and bad are mixed?
questions.answer: Take the good and leave the bad.

questions.question: What is the result of doing that?
questions.answer: He continues with peace inside.

questions.question: What does the desert stand for?
questions.answer: The world and the earth.

questions.question: What does the lion stand for?
questions.answer: Death and the appointed time.

questions.question: What does the well stand for?
questions.answer: The body and the years of life.

questions.question: What do the sixty yards help us understand?
questions.answer: The usual human lifetime of sixty years.

questions.question: What does the tree in the well stand for?
questions.answer: The period and substance of life.

questions.question: What are the white and black creatures really showing?
questions.answer: Day and night.

questions.question: What does the dragon point to?
questions.answer: The grave and the way into the next world.

questions.question: For a believer, what kind of place does the grave become?
questions.answer: A doorway from prison to a garden.

questions.question: What do the poisonous creatures mean in everyday life?
questions.answer: Hardships and calamities in the world.

questions.question: How may those hardships help a believer’s heart?
questions.answer: They can wake him up and keep him from becoming forgetful.

questions.question: What do the fruits of this world teach believers to remember?
questions.answer: The blessings waiting in the hereafter.

questions.question: Why are the fruits called examples and samples?
questions.answer: Because they are small signs of much better blessings to come.

questions.question: What does the strange one-tree-many-fruits picture prove?
questions.answer: That Allah’s power is unique and amazing.

questions.question: What is the talisman in the lesson?
questions.answer: The secret purpose of creation.

questions.question: What opens that secret for a person?
questions.answer: Belief and the words of tawhid.

questions.question: What happens to the meaning of the grave for people of the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It becomes an opening to everlasting life and Paradise.

questions.question: What does death separate misled people from?
questions.answer: From their loved ones and the world they were attached to.

questions.question: What does death bring to guided believers instead?
questions.answer: Reunion, true home, reward, and rest.

questions.question: What does the speaker want the listener not to be like?
questions.answer: The unfortunate brother.

questions.question: What does the speaker want the listener to be like?
questions.answer: The fortunate brother.

questions.question: What three things does the passage tell a person to do with the Qur’an?
questions.answer: Listen to it, obey it, and act by it.

questions.question: What truths can this story help explain after a person understands it?
questions.answer: Truths about religion, the world, human beings, and belief in Allah.

questions.question: In the meaning of the story, what does the fortunate brother represent?
questions.answer: A believing spirit and a righteous heart.

questions.question: What does the unfortunate brother represent?
questions.answer: An unbelieving spirit and a corrupt heart.

questions.question: What path is shown by the road on the right?
questions.answer: The path of the Qur’an and belief.

questions.question: What path is shown by the road on the left?
questions.answer: The path of rebellion and denial.

questions.question: What does the garden teach us about this life?
questions.answer: That good and bad are together in human life.

questions.question: Who is the sensible person in the passage?
questions.answer: The one who takes the clean good and leaves the troubling bad.

questions.question: What blessing comes to that sensible person?
questions.answer: Tranquility in the heart.

questions.question: What does the desert symbolize?
questions.answer: The earth and this world.

questions.question: What two meanings are given for the lion?
questions.answer: Death and the appointed hour.

questions.question: What two meanings are given for the well?
questions.answer: The human body and the span of life.

questions.question: What does the well’s depth point to about human life?
questions.answer: That a normal life is about sixty years.

questions.question: What does the tree symbolize?
questions.answer: The lifetime and life’s support.

questions.question: What do the two different-colored animals symbolize?
questions.answer: Night and day.

questions.question: What does the dragon symbolize?
questions.answer: The path to the Intermediate Realm and the hereafter, and its mouth means the grave.

questions.question: What does the grave become for a believer?
questions.answer: A door from the prison of this world to a garden.

questions.question: What do the poisonous vermin symbolize?
questions.answer: The calamities of worldly life.

questions.question: In what way can those calamities be good for believers?
questions.answer: They can be merciful warnings that keep them from heedlessness.

questions.question: What do the fruits on the tree symbolize?
questions.answer: Worldly blessings that point to the blessings of Paradise and the hereafter.

questions.question: What invitation do those fruits give?
questions.answer: They invite people to seek the fruits of Paradise.

questions.question: What does the many-fruited tree show about Allah?
questions.answer: It shows His special seal of power and rule.

questions.question: What does the talisman stand for?
questions.answer: The mystery of the purpose of creation.

questions.question: What is the key to that mystery?
questions.answer: Affirming Allah’s oneness and His perfect life and self-subsistence.

questions.question: What does the dragon’s mouth turning into a door teach about the grave for believers?
questions.answer: It teaches that the grave opens to mercy, immortality, and Paradise.

questions.question: What does the lion becoming gentle teach about death for believers?
questions.answer: It teaches that death becomes a friendly way to reach loved ones, home, reward, and rest.
